transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
It’s… bridges, mostly. If I know I have to cross one, before I’m even on it my heart starts pounding, my hands get damp on the wheel or the armrest, and I get this awful rush of fear.
Do you experience this kind of fear when you're in other high or open spaces, or is it mainly just bridges that cause this reaction?

Mostly bridges. I mean… I know people cross them all day and nothing happens. But if I see one coming up, or even see a high span on the map, it feels like it could just drop away underneath us. I don’t really get that same feeling everywhere else.
Have you ever had a panic attack or felt overwhelming fear in a situation that wasn't related to bridges?
Not that I can really think of. It’s… it’s mainly when a bridge is involved. I don’t usually get that sort of overwhelming fear out of the blue.
Do you often go out of your way to avoid crossing bridges because of this fear?

Yes. Quite a bit, actually. For a couple of years now I’ve planned errands and visits so I don’t have to cross them. I’ve stopped going to San Juan, and we don’t do Seattle theater nights anymore.

If I absolutely have to cross one, I need to know the route ahead of time, go at the right time, and have someone with me. Even then I’m just… frightened the whole way across.
Does your fear start as soon as you think about crossing a bridge, or does it typically begin when you're actually approaching or on the bridge?

It starts before I’m on it. Once I know crossing the bridge is unavoidable, I… I start getting scared right away. My heart pounds, my hands get damp on the wheel or the armrest. It’s already happening before we even reach the bridge.
Is your fear of crossing bridges triggered more by the thought of the bridge itself or by the act of having to cross over water or a deep chasm?
It’s more the bridge itself, I think. I know cars go over them all day, but when I see a high span on a map, or coming up through the windshield, it just feels like… it could drop away under us.
Do you feel trapped or out of control when you're in other confined or elevated spaces, like elevators or balconies?
Not really. I mean… I don’t like heights much, but I haven’t noticed the same feeling in elevators or balconies. It’s mostly when there’s a bridge involved.
Have you ever felt a similar kind of fear when you're in a situation that involves heights, but not necessarily a bridge?
I don’t think so. Not in the same way. Heights can make me a little uneasy, but… it’s not that same fear unless there’s a bridge.
Do you think your fear would be less intense if you were crossing a bridge on foot rather than in a vehicle
I don’t know that being on foot would help much. It’s seeing that high span ahead… or even on a map. I know people cross them all the time, but it still feels like it could just drop away underneath.
Is your fear of bridges more about the bridge itself as a structure, or is it about the feeling of being high up and exposed when you're on it?
It’s more the bridge itself, I think. I know plenty of cars go over them every day, but when I see a high one coming up… or even on a map… it feels like it could just drop away underneath us.
Do you think your fear of bridges is because they seem like a particularly dangerous or unpredictable situation to you?

Yes… I suppose that’s it. I know, rationally, thousands of cars go over those bridges every day. But when I see a high span ahead, or even on a map, it feels like it’s just waiting to drop away underneath us.
Do you fear other structures, like buildings or tunnels, might collapse or be dangerous in a similar way to how you fear bridges?

Not really buildings or tunnels, no. It’s mainly bridges… especially the high ones. I know cars cross them all day, but when I see one ahead, or even on a map, I get this feeling like it could just drop away underneath us.
Is your fear of bridges the same for all types of bridges, or is it worse for certain kinds, like suspension bridges or very long bridges?

It’s worse with the high spans. I don’t know that I’d sort them by type exactly… but if I see one ahead through the windshield, or even on a map, I start thinking it could just drop away underneath us, even though I know cars cross it all day.
Would your fear decrease if you were to cross a bridge that is very low to the ground, such as a small bridge over a stream?

Yes… I think so. A little bridge over a stream wouldn’t bother me the same way. It’s the high span—seeing it ahead, or even on a map—that makes it feel like it could just drop away underneath us, even though I know plenty of cars cross it every day.
Is your fear of bridges related to the height of the bridge or would you be equally afraid of crossing a bridge that is at ground level?

It’s more the height, yes. If it’s high… that’s when it gets to me. I know lots of cars go over those bridges every day, but when I see a high one ahead, or even on a map, it feels like it could just drop away underneath us.
Would you be afraid of being in a similar high position if it wasn't a bridge, such as a tall building or a mountain overlook?
I’m not sure it’s the same. It’s really the bridge… seeing that high span on the map or through the windshield. I know cars go over it all day, but it feels like it could just drop away under us.
Would your fear of bridges be significantly reduced if you were unable to see the height or the water below while crossing it?

Maybe somewhat, yes. If I couldn’t see how high it was… or the water under it… I think it would be less bad. But if I know it’s one of those high spans, even seeing it on a map or ahead of us makes me feel like it could drop away underneath, even though I know cars cross it all the time.
Is your fear of bridges equally present when crossing a bridge over land, such as a highway overpass?

If it’s just low, like a little overpass, it’s not the same. It’s when I see a high span—on the map or coming up through the windshield—that I get that feeling, like it could drop away under us, even though I know cars cross it all day.
